items.title: Conditions
items.body: Events occur independently, at a constant average rate \(\lambda\), and singly in time/space. \(X\sim\text{Po}(\lambda)\).

items.title: Mean and Variance
items.body: \(E(X)=\text{Var}(X)=\lambda\). The mean equals the variance — a key identifying feature.

items.title: Cumulative Tables
items.body: Use Poisson tables for \(P(X\leq r)\). Note \(P(X\geq r)=1-P(X\leq r-1)\). Additive: \(X+Y\sim\text{Po}(\lambda_1+\lambda_2)\).

items.title: Changing the Interval
items.body: If \(X\sim\text{Po}(\lambda)\) per hour, then in \(t\) hours: \(X\sim\text{Po}(\lambda t)\).

body.en: If events occur at a constant average rate \(\lambda\) independently, \(X\sim\text{Po}(\lambda)\) with: \(P(X=r)=\dfrac{e^{-\lambda}\lambda^r}{r!}\) for \(r=0,1,2,\ldots\)  ·  \(E(X)=\lambda\), \(\text{Var}(X)=\lambda\). Poisson approximation to Binomial: if \(n\) is large, \(p\) is small, \(np=\lambda\) is moderate (\(n>50, p<0.1\)), then \(B(n,p)\approx\text{Po}(\lambda)\).

Faults in a wire occur at a rate of 2 per metre. Find the probability of (a) exactly 3 faults in 1 m, (b) fewer than 2 faults in 0.5 m.

(a) \(\lambda=2\): \(P(X=3)=\dfrac{e^{-2}\cdot8}{6}\approx0.1804\).

(b) \(\lambda=1\): \(P(X<2)=P(0)+P(1)=e^{-1}+e^{-1}=2e^{-1}\approx0.7358\).

\(X\sim B(200,0.02)\). Use a Poisson approximation to find \(P(X=5)\).

\(\lambda=200\times0.02=4\). \(P(X=5)=\dfrac{e^{-4}\cdot4^5}{120}=\dfrac{1024e^{-4}}{120}\approx0.1563\).

question.en: Cars arrive at a toll booth at an average rate of 3 per minute. Find the probability that (a) exactly 5 arrive in one minute, (b) at least 2 arrive in 30 seconds.

label.en: ⚠️ Cambridge 9709 Traps — Linear Combinations vs Scaled Multiples in Poisson

body.en:
Sum of Independent Poisson Variables: If \(X_1 \sim \text{Po}(\lambda_1)\) and \(X_2 \sim \text{Po}(\lambda_2)\) are independent, then their sum is Poisson: \(X_1 + X_2 \sim \text{Po}(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2)\).

Scalar Multiples Are NOT Poisson: In contrast, \(2X_1\) is NOT a Poisson random variable because it can only take even integer values (0, 2, 4, ...). Its variance is \(\text{Var}(2X_1) = 4\text{Var}(X_1) = 4\lambda_1 \neq E(2X_1) = 2\lambda_1\). Always distinguish between observing two separate intervals (use \(X_1 + X_2\)) versus doubling the count of one interval (use \(2X_1\)).

question.en: The number of accidents on a highway follows a Poisson distribution with mean 1.6 per week. (a) Find the probability of at least 3 accidents in a 2-week period. (b) Given that at least one accident occurs in a week, find the probability that there are exactly 2 accidents in that week.

solution.en:
(a) In a 2-week period, the parameter scales to \(\lambda = 1.6 \times 2 = 3.2\):

\[P(X \ge 3) = 1 - P(X \le 2) = 1 - e^{-3.2}\left(1 + 3.2 + \frac{3.2^2}{2}\right) = 1 - 9.32e^{-3.2} \approx 1 - 0.3799 = 0.620\text{ (3 s.f.)}\]

(b) For 1 week, \(\lambda = 1.6\). Use conditional probability:

\[P(X = 2 \mid X \ge 1) = \frac{P(X = 2)}{P(X \ge 1)} = \frac{\frac{e^{-1.6}(1.6)^2}{2}}{1 - e^{-1.6}} = \frac{1.28e^{-1.6}}{1 - e^{-1.6}} \approx \frac{0.2584}{0.7981} \approx 0.324\text{ (3 s.f.)}\]
